title: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw, warns exploits may surface quickly
content_md: The Drupal Security Team has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability that can let attackers take over vulnerable sites. This content management system (CMS) is commonly used by large organizations that manage multi-site installations and massive data structures, including government entities, educational organizations, major research universities, and high-profile enterprise and media organizations. The security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-132165) was discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner , and anonymous users can exploit it to reinstall the Drupal CMS. "Drupal core ships with an install.php file for installing Drupal core. Under specific conditions, an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal. This can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution," the Drupal Security Team warned in a Wednesday advisory. "Some exploit paths are mitigated if the web server cannot write to or change permissions on settings.php." Admins whose websites use the paid Drupal Steward Web Application Firewall (WAF) service are already protected from known attack vectors, but should still upgrade to Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13 in case other attack vectors are discovered. Those who can't immediately upgrade should secure the Drupal installer by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file in the web root.
